title: Roman consensus — Christ and Apostles taught unwritten faith and worship matters
source_text: IX. Etenim Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae communi consensu docent, Christum Dominum nostrum, & Apostolos ejus, multa docuisse & instituisse ad fidem & divinum cultum pertinentia, quae in sacris literis expressa non reperiuntur, nec sufficienter inde possunt erui: adeoque doctrinam Christianam & Apostolicam partim Scriptura, partim verbo quodam non scripto, & ore tenus tradito contineri.
pass_a_gloss: For the doctors of the Roman Church teach by common consent that Christ our Lord and his Apostles taught and instituted many things belonging to faith and divine worship which are not found expressed in the sacred letters and cannot be sufficiently drawn from them: and therefore that Christian and Apostolic doctrine is contained partly in Scripture, partly in a certain unwritten word handed on by oral tradition.
pass_b_english: Roman doctors agree: Christ and the Apostles taught and set up many points of faith and worship that sacred Scripture neither states expressly nor yields sufficiently when mined alone.
Christian and Apostolic doctrine, on their view, rests partly on Scripture and partly on an unwritten word passed along by mouth.

lemmas.gloss: handed on by oral tradition / by mouth
can be sufficiently drawn from there

choices.why: Marks the unwritten deposit Roman side pairs with Scripture.
Same verb family as Roman denial in VIII against sola Scriptura extraction.
